Nathan A. Schwadron is verified as a Professor at the University of New Hampshire, affiliated with the College of Engineering and Physical Sciences (CEPS) and the Institute for the Study of Earth, Oceans, and Space (EOS), and specifically with the UNH Space Science Center (SSC) heliophysics program. His listed UNH contacts match the lead record: email Nathan.Schwadron@unh.edu (canonical form; lead gave the alias n.schwadron@unh.edu), phone (603) 862-3451, office Morse Hall Room 350, Durham NH 03824. ORCID 0000-0002-3737-9283 is registered on his LANL profile. Per LinkedIn, he has held the UNH Professor title continuously since September 2010. He is also listed as a Visiting Research Collaborator at Princeton University and a Research Scientist at Los Alamos National Laboratory — these are secondary affiliations preserved across his profile but his primary appointment, and the only one tied to UNH, is the SSC professorship. His research-stream concentration is unambiguously heliophysics: solar wind, pickup ions, suprathermal particles, the heliospheric magnetic field, the heliospheric boundary, galactic cosmic ray environments and radiation hazards for space exploration.

Research.com lists him as Nathan A. Schwadron, University of New Hampshire, Physics D-Index 81 (ranked ~2787 world, ~1334 US) with 839 publications and 23,562 citations, consistent with a senior, active heliophysics PI.

### Pre-2024 NSF Competitive Grants Disclosed (Out of Scope — Listed for Reference Only)

| 2102866 / FESD-2102866 (Grantome: "FESD Type 1: Sun to Ice—Impacts on Earth of Extreme Solar Events") | Sun to Ice: Impacts on Earth of Extreme Solar Events | NSF | Schwadron (Co-PI) | $5,000,000 (overall FESD) | 2011 |

**Implication:** None of these pre-2024 awards meets the funding-scope criteria. No public 2024-current record of a new competitive grant was discoverable in the canonical federal award databases (NSF, NSPIRES, USASpending) at the lead's verified institutional identity.

**Mechanism:** Heliophysics PIs of Schwadron's seniority typically receive NASA ROSES awards (HSR, HDE, SR, ECIP) as Co-Is on team proposals led from other institutions (e.g., Princeton-led IMAP science, Caltech-led LWS). These Co-I subawards flow through the lead institution directly to UNH Sponsored Programs and may not appear in the Co-Is-only public search index of NSPIRES or NSF.

### Mission / Consortium Activity (Distinct from Competitive Grants)

UNH is a longstanding partner institute on NASA's Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP) mission, for which Schwadron has been associated with instrument science work (interstellar dust / energetic particles). IMAP launched on 2025-09-24 and began its two-year primary science mission on 2026-02-02. NASA mission budgets flow through the prime institution (Princeton PI David McComas, spacecraft by APL) and are not personal grants to Schwadron. The NSF New England Space Science Consortium (which Schwadron created and formerly led) is institution-level support, also not a personal grant.

**Action / Recommendation:** To verify team-level 2024-2026 NASA grants where Schwadron is a Co-I/Co-PI (rather than lead PI), request via NSPIRES the underlying award list filtered by co-investigator rather than PI, or pull the ROSES HSR/HDE selection lists for 2023-2025 and grep for "Schwadron" in Co-I blocks.
